01 The idea

Elephants crossing into farmland cost lives, crops and homes. EleGuard places seismic sensor nodes along wildlife corridors. When the ground shakes the way a large animal makes it shake, the system alerts the villagers and rangers in that zone and plans a drone route to turn the animals back before they reach the houses. Built as a team final-year project.

  • 4steps: detect, alert, respond, track
  • 3kinds of node: seismic, village, drone
  • 1live map for every incident

02 What it does

01

Detect

Seismic nodes along the corridor pick up the vibration pattern of large animals moving.

02

Alert the right people

Only the villagers and rangers in that sensor's zone are notified, by SMS, email or push.

03

Plan the response

A drone flight plan is generated to reach the animals and turn them back.

04

Live incident map

Active alerts, sensor health and drone missions on one screen.

05

Sensor registry

Every node registered with its GPS position and linked to the villages it faces.

06

History and patterns

Every event, alert and mission logged, to map where conflict happens.

03 Under the hood

For the technical reader: how it is put together.

  • NestJS
  • PostgreSQL
  • MQTT
  • Socket.io
  • BullMQ
  • Redis
  • React 19
  • Vite
  1. Nodes publish over MQTT 5 to a HiveMQ broker. The NestJS backend turns events into alerts.
  2. Socket.io pushes detections to the dashboard the moment they arrive.
  3. BullMQ and Redis queue notifications and drone missions.
  4. React 19, Vite and Tailwind on the dashboard. Simulators stand in for real nodes during development.
